title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
notes: The convergence-speed and learning-rate claims are mechanism claims that should survive shrinking. The ImageNet numbers do not. Note that the paper's stated explanation -- internal covariate shift -- was later disputed by Santurkar et al. (2018); that is a claim about why, which reduced-scale testing cannot settle either way, so it is annotated as not testable rather than as false.

claims.text: A batch-normalized network reaches a given accuracy in fewer training steps than the same network without batch normalization.
claims.notes: Convergence speed on a small convnet; the mechanism is not scale dependent.

claims.text: Batch normalization allows training with a much higher learning rate without the network diverging.
claims.notes: Directly testable: train both arms at a learning rate that diverges without batch norm.

claims.text: Batch normalization acts as a regulariser, so dropout can be removed or reduced without losing accuracy.
claims.notes: A claim of no difference. At reduced scale with three seeds, absence of a difference is inconclusive rather than confirmation.

claims.text: Batch normalization achieves the same accuracy as the original Inception model with 14 times fewer training steps.
claims.notes: A specific speedup factor on an ImageNet-scale model.

claims.text: An ensemble of batch-normalized networks reaches 4.9% top-5 validation error on ImageNet.
claims.notes: A headline number requiring ImageNet training.

claims.text: The benefit of batch normalization comes from reducing internal covariate shift.
claims.notes: A causal explanation, not an experimental comparison between two arms. Later work (Santurkar et al. 2018) disputed it. Reduced-scale testing measures whether the effect holds, not why.

claims.text: Batch normalization makes training less sensitive to the scale of the weight initialisation.
claims.notes: Testable by varying initialisation scale across both arms.
